raw_response:
Thirty years I have been working this land. I do not read books about farming — I watch what the people around me do, and I remember what worked last year and what did not.

My 12.4 mu I split like this: about 8 mu I rotate wheat and maize together — same ground, wheat in winter, maize in summer. The other 4 mu I put into stevia. A few years back I started the stevia because the company comes and buys the leaves and the price is steady. My neighbor Mrs. Zhang does it too and she makes decent money, so I followed her.

**Wheat (8 mu, sown October, harvested June):**
I buy improved seed every year — everyone in our village does now, the old varieties give less. Before I sow I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, that 45% kind, then in spring around jointing time I spread maybe 20 jin of urea per mu as a chase fertilizer. I do this by hand, walking the rows. I irrigate three times — once after sowing to get germination, once in spring when it starts growing fast, once at heading. I spray once for weeds early on and once more for rust and aphids near the end. I use the rotary tiller my nephew rents out before sowing. I expect around 450 jin per mu, maybe 500 if the winter is not too cold.

**Maize (8 mu, sown June, harvested September):**
Right after wheat harvest I go straight to maize — I cannot wait long because the season is short. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958, same as my neighbor Old Wang uses, he gets good ears. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then when the plants reach my waist I add 40 jin of urea per mu in two goes. I water twice — once at planting and once when the silk comes out. I spray herbicide once early and watch for corn borer, I spray one more time if I see them. Rotary tillage again, quick pass before planting. I figure 550–600 jin per mu most years.

**Stevia (4 mu, year-round, harvested multiple cuts):**
This one I learned mostly from Mrs. Zhang and what the company people told her. I put half a bag of compound per mu in spring, then after each cutting I add a little urea — about 15 jin per mu — to push regrowth. I water more than the grain crops, about four or five times through the season since stevia wilts fast if the ground dries out. I spray once or twice for bugs. I rotary till before planting in spring. I get maybe three cuttings of leaves, total around 200 jin dry per mu if I manage it well.
